So the backend can't resolve auth.localhost either → JWKS fetch fails → 503. This is an environment/DNS issue.

But wait - is this a genuine installation failure, or just sandbox DNS? The guide says access at localhost:3000 with Keycloak at auth.localhost:3000. However the actual backend config in local.yaml uses auth.localhost... The app relies on hostname resolution. In a normal dev machine, *.localhost resolves to 127.0.0.1 automatically (many systems). Here getent hosts auth.localhost returns nothing.

Hmm. Actually, is this the real cause? The backend got a 503 auth.idp_unavailable. Let me check whether the backend also needs the JWKS from Keycloak. The token was issued fine through Traefik via Host header. The backend itself is trying to reach issuer_url http://auth.localhost:3000. If DNS fails, JWKS unavailable.

But wait, this could be a validation environment quirk. Actually the standard setup: docker with traefik. Backend runs on the host (not container) per run-dev. Local dev on macOS: *.localhost resolves. On Linux, systemd-resolved resolves *.localhost? Actually glibc's NSS doesn't automatically resolve subdomains of localhost; but many distros have `localhost` only. Hmm.
